title: Clinical Data Managers
description: Apply knowledge of health care and database management to analyze clinical data, and to identify and report trends.

tasks.text: Monitor work productivity or quality to ensure compliance with standard operating procedures.
Track the flow of work forms, including in-house data flow or electronic forms transfer.
Design and validate clinical databases, including designing or testing logic checks.
Process clinical data, including receipt, entry, verification, or filing of information.
Generate data queries, based on validation checks or errors and omissions identified during data entry, to resolve identified problems.
Perform quality control audits to ensure accuracy, completeness, or proper usage of clinical systems and data.
Analyze clinical data using appropriate statistical tools.
Evaluate processes and technologies, and suggest revisions to increase productivity and efficiency.
Read technical literature and participate in continuing education or professional associations to maintain awareness of current database technology and best practices.
Develop or select specific software programs for various research scenarios.
Develop project-specific data management plans that address areas such as coding, reporting, or transfer of data, database locks, and work flow processes.
Prepare appropriate formatting to data sets as requested.
Design forms for receiving, processing, or tracking data.
Prepare data analysis listings and activity, performance, or progress reports.
Develop technical specifications for data management programming and communicate needs to information technology staff.
Write work instruction manuals, data capture guidelines, or standard operating procedures.
Confer with end users to define or implement clinical system requirements such as data release formats, delivery schedules, and testing protocols.
Supervise the work of data management project staff.
Contribute to the compilation, organization, and production of protocols, clinical study reports, regulatory submissions, or other controlled documentation.
Train staff on technical procedures or software program usage.
Provide support and information to functional areas such as marketing, clinical monitoring, and medical affairs.

skills.name: Critical Thinking
skills.def: Using logic and reasoning to identify the strengths and weaknesses of alternative solutions, conclusions, or approaches to problems.

skills.name: Reading Comprehension
skills.def: Understanding written sentences and paragraphs in work-related documents.

skills.name: Active Listening
skills.def: Giving full attention to what other people are saying, taking time to understand the points being made, asking questions as appropriate, and not interrupting at inappropriate times.

skills.name: Speaking
skills.def: Talking to others to convey information effectively.

skills.name: Writing
skills.def: Communicating effectively in writing as appropriate for the needs of the audience.

skills.name: Active Learning
skills.def: Understanding the implications of new information for both current and future problem-solving and decision-making.

skills.name: Monitoring
skills.def: Monitoring/Assessing performance of yourself, other individuals, or organizations to make improvements or take corrective action.

skills.name: Mathematics
skills.def: Using mathematics to solve problems.

skills.name: Complex Problem Solving
skills.def: Identifying complex problems and reviewing related information to develop and evaluate options and implement solutions.

skills.name: Coordination
skills.def: Adjusting actions in relation to others' actions.

skills.name: Time Management
skills.def: Managing one's own time and the time of others.

skills.name: Programming
skills.def: Writing computer programs for various purposes.

skills.name: Judgment and Decision Making
skills.def: Considering the relative costs and benefits of potential actions to choose the most appropriate one.

skills.name: Systems Analysis
skills.def: Determining how a system should work and how changes in conditions, operations, and the environment will affect outcomes.

skills.name: Social Perceptiveness
skills.def: Being aware of others' reactions and understanding why they react as they do.

skills.name: Systems Evaluation
skills.def: Identifying measures or indicators of system performance and the actions needed to improve or correct performance, relative to the goals of the system.

skills.name: Instructing
skills.def: Teaching others how to do something.

skills.name: Management of Personnel Resources
skills.def: Motivating, developing, and directing people as they work, identifying the best people for the job.

skills.name: Learning Strategies
skills.def: Selecting and using training/instructional methods and procedures appropriate for the situation when learning or teaching new things.

skills.name: Persuasion
skills.def: Persuading others to change their minds or behavior.

skills.name: Data base user interface and query software
skills.def: Software to query, present, or edit information stored in a database sytem. Examples: 5AM Glassbox Translational Research, ClearTrial, Clinical trial management software, DZS Software Solutions ClinPlus.

skills.name: Medical software
skills.def: Software to evaluate, plan, or redesign healthcare procedures. May include reporting or visualization features. Examples: Allscripts healthcare automation software, Epic Systems, EpicCare Ambulatory Electronic Medical Records (EMR) software, MEDITECH software.

skills.name: Spreadsheet software
skills.def: Software to create or edit numbers or text organized into rows and columns of cells. May include formulas which recalculate values based on other cells. Examples: Microsoft Excel.

skills.name: Office suite software
skills.def: Software to provide word processing, spreadsheet, e-mail, presentations, or data management capabilities. Examples: Microsoft Office software.

skills.name: Presentation software
skills.def: Software to create presentations, speeches, or slideshows. Examples: Microsoft PowerPoint.

skills.name: Object or component oriented development software
skills.def: Software to create or maintain applications using object-oriented programming concepts. Examples: C#, C++, Oracle Java.
